items.passage:
If the conduct of the men had been alarming in the boat, it became truly threatening when they had come aboard. They lay about the deck growling together in talk. The slightest order was received with a black look, and grudgingly and carelessly obeyed. Even the honest hands must have caught the infection, for there was not one man aboard to mend another. Mutiny, it was plain, hung over us like a thunder-cloud.

And it was not only we of the cabin party who perceived the danger. Long John was hard at work going from group to group, spending himself in good advice, and as for example no man could have shown a better.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “hung over us like a thunder-cloud” most nearly suggests that
options: the crew had already openly seized control of the ship
a dangerous revolt seemed ready to break out at any moment
stormy weather was delaying the progress of the voyage
the sailors were grieving over companions lost at sea
items.explanation: 'thunder-cloud'는 아직 터지지 않았지만 곧 쏟아질 듯한 위협을 비유한다. 앞 문장들에서 선원들이 투덜거리고 명령에 험악한 표정으로 마지못해 따른다고 하여 반란의 기운이 감돌고 있음을 보여 준다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 반란이 이미 일어났다고 보아 틀리고, C는 비유를 실제 날씨로 읽은 오류이며, D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Several gentlemen were under the necessity last night of sleeping in the brick fields, and on the steps of doors, for which they were taken before the magistrates in a body this morning, and committed to prison as vagrants for various terms. One of these persons I understand to be a highly-respectable tinker, of great practical skill, who had forwarded a paper to the President of Section D. Mechanical Science, on the construction of pipkins with copper bottoms and safety-values, of which report speaks highly. The incarceration of this gentleman is greatly to be ______, as his absence will preclude any discussion on the subject.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에서 이 신사가 없으므로 그 주제에 대한 토론이 불가능해진다고 말한다. 또한 그의 논문이 높이 평가받는다고 했으므로 그의 투옥은 아쉬운 일이다. 따라서 C 'regretted'가 정답이다. A와 D는 투옥을 긍정적으로 보는 말이라 맞지 않고, B는 아쉬움이라는 평가를 담지 못한다.

items.passage:
The print must indeed have been large and clear, for the twilight was fading fast.

She looked up and met his glance with direct and steady eyes of a clear grey. A severe critic of that which none can satisfactorily define--a woman's beauty--would have objected that her face was too wide, and her chin too square. Her hair, which was of a bright brown, grew with a singular strength and crispness round a brow which was serene and square. In her eyes there shone the light of ______, and a steady purpose. A student of human nature must have regretted that the soul looking out of such eyes should have been vouchsafed to a woman. For strength and purpose in a man are usually exercised for the good of mankind, while in a woman such qualities must, it would seem, benefit no more than one man of her own generation, and a few who may follow her in the next.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: 빈칸 바로 뒤에 'and a steady purpose'가 이어져 굳은 의지를 나타내는 말이 필요하다. 앞의 'direct and steady eyes'와 뒤의 'strength and purpose'도 같은 성격을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 D 'tenacity'가 정답이다. A는 반대 의미이고, B와 C는 지문의 묘사와 관련이 없다.

items.passage:
When Sepeli dropped both pig and Chancellor, a talking man from the windward coast picked up the carcass. Cornelius was on his feet and running, when the pig caught him on the legs and tripped him. The people and the army, with shouts and laughter, joined in the sport.

Twist and dodge as he would, everywhere the ex-Chancellor of the Exchequer was met or overtaken by the flying pig. He scuttled like a frightened rabbit in and out among the avocados and the palms. No hand was laid upon him, and his tormentors made way before him, but ever they pursued, and ever the pig flew as fast as hands could pick it up.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “scuttled like a frightened rabbit” most nearly suggests that
options: moved in a hurried, panicked way to escape his pursuers
carefully planned a clever route to a safe hiding place
enjoyed the lively game as much as the crowd did
waited quietly among the trees until the crowd tired
items.explanation: 'frightened rabbit'는 겁에 질려 이리저리 급히 달아나는 모습을 비유한다. 앞에서 그가 몸을 비틀고 피하려 해도 돼지에 계속 쫓긴다고 묘사되어 있다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 계획성을, C는 즐거움을, D는 가만히 기다림을 말해 지문의 다급한 도주와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
During the short period of silence their victims could not tell what they were about. They only knew, by occasional sounds reaching them from above, that there was some change in the performance; but what it was they could not even shape a conjecture.

The interregnum at length ended with a loud rumbling noise, that was itself suddenly terminated by a grand crash, as if a portion of the impending cliff had become detached, and fallen down upon the platform.

Then succeeded a silence, unbroken by the slightest sound. No longer was heard either noise or voice--not the murmur of one.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “as if a portion of the impending cliff had become detached” most nearly suggests that
options: the cliff above the platform had truly begun to collapse
the crash was so loud and heavy that it resembled falling rock
the victims had heard someone climbing down the cliff
the silence afterward came from rocks blocking the sound
items.explanation: 'as if'는 실제 사실이 아니라 소리의 크기를 비교하는 표현이다. 앞에서 'a loud rumbling noise'와 'a grand crash'가 언급되어 바위가 떨어지는 듯한 굉음임을 보여 준다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 비유를 실제 붕괴로 읽은 오류이고, C와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
As the words passed her lips there rose a sound of running feet, and through the open door at the far end of the hall burst in a score or over of armed men. Then at last Sir Andrew saw and understood.

With a roar of ______ like that of a wounded lion, he seized his daughter and dragged her back with him down the passage into the solar where a fire burned and lights had been lit ready for their retiring, flinging to and bolting the door behind them.

“Swift!” he said, as he tore his gown from him, “there is no escape, but at least I can die fighting for you. Give me my mail.”

She snatched his hauberk from the wall, and while they thundered at the door, did it on to him—ay, and his steel helm also, and gave him his long sword and his shield.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 'like that of a wounded lion'은 상처 입은 사자처럼 사납게 울부짖는 모습을 나타낸다. 이어서 그는 문을 걸어 잠그고 싸우다 죽겠다고 말한다. 따라서 분노를 뜻하는 C 'rage'가 정답이다. A, B, D는 무장한 적이 몰려오는 위급한 장면과 어울리지 않는다.

items.passage:
The sands were wet, and unpleasant to walk on; and she was not sorry. What did it matter? She was in the frame of mind to experience a sort of malicious enjoyment of outward miseries. The tryst looked melancholy enough when she reached it. She made her way to the nook, behind the sheltering rocks, and stood there, looking out to sea. She had not expected to find the place wearing its summer aspect, but she was scarcely prepared to face such ______. Everything was gray--gray tossing sea, gray screaming gulls, gray lowering sky.

“It would have been better to have stayed at home,” she said.

Still she could not make up her mind to turn back at once, and lingered a little, leaning against a rock, shivering, and feeling dreary; and so it was that the man who was approaching first caught sight of her figure.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: 빈칸 바로 뒤에서 바다, 갈매기, 하늘이 모두 회색이라고 묘사한다. 앞에서도 그 장소가 'melancholy enough'해 보였다고 한다. 따라서 황량함을 뜻하는 D 'desolateness'가 정답이다. A와 C는 여름 풍경에 어울리는 말이고, B는 아무도 없는 장소와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
The King sent for the bonds and upon close scrutiny discovered that one of them was on paper bearing the water-mark of a mill that was not built till two years after the date written in the bond. The noble was arrested and the search of his house brought to light several similar documents waiting their turn. He went to the scaffold. His rank only aggravated his offence in the eyes of the King. No wonder the fame of this judge spread quickly through the land.

A dozen contented years he reigned in peace, doing justice between man and man at home.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the fame of this judge spread quickly through the land” most nearly suggests that
options: word of the judge's wisdom became widely known throughout the kingdom
the judge traveled quickly from one region to another
the judge's harsh sentences frightened people into leaving
the noble's family quickly spread rumors against the judge
items.explanation: 'spread'는 명성이 물이 번지듯 퍼져 나간다는 비유이다. 앞에서 판사가 종이의 워터마크로 위조를 밝혀낸 일이 묘사되어 그의 지혜가 널리 알려질 이유가 드러난다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 판사의 실제 이동으로 읽은 오류이며, C와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
The sergeant gave the order and moved to his place on the right of the company, leaving the captain in command. His first move was to open the ranks, and his next to order the quartermaster-sergeant to supply each man with ten rounds of ammunition. Candor compels us to say that the sergeant did not strictly ______ this order. He was careful to put ten cartridges, and no more, into each box, but he did not scruple to put three or four extra ones into the hand that was holding the box open.

By this time the boys had found out who was to be their real commander.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에서 상사는 상자에는 정확히 열 발만 넣었지만 손에는 서너 발을 더 쥐여 주었다고 한다. 이는 명령을 엄격히 따르지 않았다는 뜻이므로 B 'obey'가 정답이다. A는 명령에 이의를 제기한 장면이 없어 맞지 않고, C와 D는 그가 명령 내용을 알고 일부 지킨 사실과 어긋난다.

items.passage:
In the country school I attended, there was a debating society. Parents as well as their sons were admitted to the society and the public was invited to the debates. On one occasion the question for debate was: "Which is the more attractive, the works of nature or the works of art?"

There had been an appeal from a general debate and this time one speaker was chosen from each side. My father was chosen to represent the negative and I the affirmative. My father was a good speaker but so fond of facts he had no use for rhetoric. I had the opening address of thirty minutes, my father had forty-five minutes and I had fifteen minutes to close the debate.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “had no use for rhetoric” most nearly suggests that
options: could not afford to pay for training in public speaking
lacked the books he needed to prepare his speech
cared little for ornate, persuasive language in his arguments
had grown tired of joining debates at the school
items.explanation: 'had no use for'는 실제로 쓸 수 없다는 뜻이 아니라 가치를 두지 않는다는 관용 표현이다. 바로 앞의 'so fond of facts'와 대조되어 그가 꾸밈 있는 말보다 사실을 중시했음을 보여 준다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 돈이나 자료 부족으로 읽은 오류이고, D는 그가 토론에 참여했다는 사실과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Desperate with fear, I rushed forward with an unceremonious, "You must permit me, Sir--" and felt him. My Wife was right. There was not the trace of an angle, not the slightest roughness or inequality: never in my life had I met with a more perfect Circle. He remained motionless while I walked round him, beginning from his eye and returning to it again. Circular he was throughout, a perfectly satisfactory Circle; there could not be a doubt of it. Then followed a dialogue, which I will endeavour to set down as near as I can recollect it, omitting only some of my profuse apologies--for I was covered with ______ and humiliation that I, a Square, should have been guilty of the impertinence of feeling a Circle.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 'and humiliation'과 짝을 이루는 감정이 필요하다. 앞의 'profuse apologies'와 'guilty of the impertinence'도 화자가 부끄러워하고 있음을 보여 준다. 따라서 D 'shame'이 정답이다. A와 B는 긍정적 감정이라 맞지 않고, C는 사과하는 태도와 어울리지 않는다.

items.passage:
The nobility of the oak casts the pitiful laurel into utter insignificance. With elms it is the same; they are reddish with flower and bud very early in the year, the fresh leaf is a tender green; in autumn they are sometimes one mass of yellow.

Ashes change from almost black to a light green, then a deeper green, and again light green and yellow. Where is the foreign evergreen in the competition? Put side by side, competition is out of the question; you have only to get an artist to paint the oak in its three phases to see this.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “casts the pitiful laurel into utter insignificance” most nearly suggests that
options: the laurel seems unimportant when it is compared with the oak
the oak's broad branches shade the laurel from sunlight
the oak's roots slowly destroy the laurel growing nearby
gardeners throw away laurels to make room for oaks
items.explanation: 'casts … into insignificance'는 비교를 통해 상대를 하찮아 보이게 만든다는 비유이다. 뒤에서 'competition is out of the question'이라며 외래 상록수가 토종 나무와 비교가 안 된다고 말한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B, C, D는 'casts'를 실제 물리적 행위로 읽은 오류이다.

items.passage: To the left of us there was the long uninterrupted shoal, and to the right a high, steep bank heavily overgrown with bushes. Above the bush the trees stood in serried ranks. The twigs overhung the current thickly, and from distance to distance a large limb of some tree projected rigidly over the stream. It was then well on in the afternoon, the face of the forest was ______, and a broad strip of shadow had already fallen on the water. In this shadow we steamed up—very slowly, as you may imagine.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: 빈칸 바로 뒤에서 넓은 그림자가 이미 물 위에 드리웠다고 말한다. 앞에서도 나무들이 빽빽이 서 있고 가지가 물 위로 늘어져 있다고 묘사한다. 따라서 어둡다는 뜻의 B 'gloomy'가 정답이다. A는 그림자와 반대되고, C와 D는 지문의 묘사와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Beyond all that, the situation was a commanding one. The prospect from almost every window was beautiful. Hillsides covered with thrifty crops—maple groves that became gorgeous in the autumn—farm-houses that gave an idea of elegance as well as comfort, formed lovely rural pictures whereon the inmates of the institution looked. Indeed, within or without, there was nothing to excite the brain or give an unpleasant emotion. Authority there was, certainly, firm and judicious, but so concealed in all its rugged points, that even the sharp suspicion of insanity failed to jar against it. Indeed, the ruling spirit of this place was Mrs. Barr, whose charity was ever prevailing, and whose firm goodness was rendered efficient by proportionate strength. To her the inmates of this building were objects of unlimited interest.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the ruling spirit of this place was Mrs. Barr” most nearly suggests that
options: Mrs. Barr was a ghost said to haunt the institution
Mrs. Barr held a title but had no real influence
Mrs. Barr was the guiding influence that shaped the place
Mrs. Barr's changing moods controlled the inmates
items.explanation: 'ruling spirit'는 유령이 아니라 그곳을 이끄는 중심 인물을 뜻한다. 뒤에서 그녀의 자비와 굳은 선함이 효과적으로 작용했다고 하고, 앞에서 권위가 부드럽게 감춰져 있었다고 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 'spirit'를 문자 그대로 읽은 오류이고, B와 D는 지문의 긍정적 묘사와 어긋난다.

items.passage:
A thing which even she, a landswoman, a girl originally unacquainted with anything connected with seafaring matters, had, by now, come to recognise and understand as vital to all on board that ship. She had felt the back of the straw hat she wore lifted by a slight warm ______ of air, while, at the same moment, some of the pages of a book she had left lying on the table were suddenly turned over swiftly and with a loud rustle.

'It is the breeze,' she muttered, 'the breeze! The wind at last!'

The others on deck had perceived it as quickly as she.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 'of air'와 앞의 'slight warm'이 가볍게 일렁이는 공기의 움직임을 가리킨다. 이어 책장이 바스락 넘어가고 그녀가 바람이 분다고 외친다. 따라서 D 'ripple'이 정답이다. A는 움직임이 없는 것이고, B와 C는 공기를 묘사하는 말로 어색하다.

items.passage: I had faltered, and my cause was lost. What have I accomplished? Am I able to gloat over you? What have I wrought, after all? I weakened under the love she bore for you, I permitted it to creep in and fill my heart. Do you understand? I do not hate you now. It is something to know that you have worshipped her all these years. You were true to her. What you did long, long ago was not your fault. You believed that she had wronged you. But you went on loving her. That is what weakened my resolve. You loved her to the end, she loved you to the end. Well, in the face of that, could I go on hating you? You must have been worthy of her love.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “permitted it to creep in and fill my heart” most nearly suggests that
options: the speaker's feelings changed gradually, almost without notice
the speaker suddenly decided to forgive in a single moment
the speaker felt fear of someone sneaking into the house
the speaker tried hard to hide his love from others
items.explanation: 'creep in'은 조용히 조금씩 스며드는 모습을 비유한다. 앞에서 화자는 자신이 'faltered'했다고 하고, 뒤에서는 그 사랑 때문에 결심이 약해져 더 이상 미워하지 않는다고 말한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 점진적 변화와 반대이고, C는 비유를 실제 침입으로 읽은 오류이며, D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: The Scotch yeoman was a man of another sort. He possessed straightforward ______ and common sense approaching to sagacity in his slowness and solidity of intellect. He was further endowed with some of the delicacy of feeling and action in which those fine gentlemen of fiction are often curiously deficient. He knew perfectly well that it was not in his honorary office of farm-manager to go much about the young Lady of Drumsheugh and attempt to control her in her domestic concerns. To do so would be to draw down upon both the strongly-flavoured gossip of the country side.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 'straightforward'는 솔직하고 곧은 성품을 나타낸다. 뒤에서도 그가 섬세한 감정을 지니고 자신의 직분을 넘지 않을 줄 안다고 묘사한다. 따라서 B 'honesty'가 정답이다. A와 C는 부정적 성품으로 칭찬하는 문맥과 맞지 않고, D는 'common sense'와 함께 나열되기 어렵다.

items.passage: Many of these are secretly for us. They would join me, but they fear to do so lest their estates be confiscated. These are to be assured that what they may lose now by aiding me shall some day be restored to them. Here is a list of a number of such gentlemen in the province of Berry, and you are to give them the assurances necessary to enlist them in our cause. Use what persuasions you can. Take your company, and find some place of concealment among the hills of the southern border of Berry. You can thus provide escort in crossing the border for those who may need it.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “enlist them in our cause” most nearly suggests that
options: sign them up as soldiers in the royal army
write their names on an official list for the province
persuade them to openly join and support the effort
force them to give up their estates to the leader
items.explanation: 'enlist'는 원래 군에 입대시킨다는 뜻이지만 여기서는 대의에 동참하도록 설득한다는 의미로 쓰였다. 바로 뒤의 'Use what persuasions you can'과 앞의 그들이 몰래 지지하지만 두려워한다는 설명이 이를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 단어를 문자 그대로 읽은 오류이고, D는 재산을 돌려주겠다는 약속과 어긋난다.

items.passage:
Touched by my Wife's distress, I would have sprung downward to reassure her, but I found myself incapable of motion. "Trouble not yourself about your Wife," said my Guide: "she will not be long left in anxiety; meantime, let us take a survey of Flatland."

Once more I felt myself rising through space. It was even as the Sphere had said. The further we receded from the object we beheld, the ______ became the field of vision. My native city, with the interior of every house and every creature therein, lay open to my view in miniature.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: 빈칸 앞에서 바라보는 대상으로부터 멀어질수록이라고 말한다. 뒤에서는 도시 전체와 모든 집 안이 축소된 모습으로 한눈에 보였다고 한다. 따라서 시야가 넓어졌다는 뜻의 D 'larger'가 정답이다. A는 반대 의미이고, B와 C는 멀어지며 한눈에 보인다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.
